sql: select 'null_supply_cost_customers' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as reference_value

description: Max lifetime_orders value for any single customer (top-end outlier check).
sql: select 'max_lifetime_orders' as slice, (select max(lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select max(lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Count of customers with negative lifetime_revenue, which should not occur if refunds are properly excluded.
sql: select 'negative_revenue_customers' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_revenue < 0) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_revenue < 0) as reference_value

description: Checks internal consistency: count of model rows where avg_order_value does not equal lifetime_revenue/lifetime_orders within tolerance, compared to same check on reference.
sql: select 'avg_order_value_inconsistent_rows' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where abs(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue::double / lifetime_orders) > 0.01) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where abs(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue::double / lifetime_orders) > 0.01) as reference_value

description: Sum of lifetime_revenue bucketed by lifetime_orders (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+) to find fan-out or filter issues concentrated in certain order-count ranges.
sql: with m as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(m.bucket, r.bucket) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.bucket = r.bucket

description: Count of customers bucketed by lifetime_orders range.
sql: with m as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(m.bucket, r.bucket) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.bucket = r.bucket

description: Average of avg_order_supply_cost restricted to customers with non-null, non-zero values in both tables, isolating cases where null-exclusion logic may differ.
sql: select 'avg_supply_cost_nonzero_nonnull' as slice, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null and avg_order_supply_cost != 0) as model_value, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null and avg_order_supply_cost != 0) as reference_value

description: Count of rows per customer_name to detect potential name collisions/join fan-out distinct from customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_name, r.customer_name) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from (select customer_name, count(*) as v from model_output group by 1) m full outer join (select customer_name, count(*) as v from reference_output group by 1) r on m.customer_name = r.customer_name

description: Count of customers whose first_order_date equals last_order_date (single-day customers), a boundary condition.
sql: select 'first_eq_last_order_date' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where first_order_date = last_order_date) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where first_order_date = last_order_date) as reference_value

description: Count of customers per last_order_date near the most recent day, to catch as-of/cutoff boundary mismatches.
sql: with bounds as (select greatest((select max(last_order_date) from model_output), (select max(last_order_date) from reference_output)) as max_d) select coalesce(m.d, r.d) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from (select cast(last_order_date as varchar) as d, count(*) as v from model_output, bounds where last_order_date >= bounds.max_d - 7 group by 1) m full outer join (select cast(last_order_date as varchar) as d, count(*) as v from reference_output, bounds where last_order_date >= bounds.max_d - 7 group by 1) r on m.d = r.d

description: Count of customers with lifetime_orders = 0 but non-null revenue, which should not occur (sanity check).
sql: select 'zero_orders_nonzero_revenue' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_orders = 0 and lifetime_revenue is not null and lifetime_revenue != 0) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_orders = 0 and lifetime_revenue is not null and lifetime_revenue != 0) as reference_value

description: Count of customers where lifetime_revenue differs by more than 1 cent between model and reference.
sql: select 'revenue_mismatch_gt_1cent' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where abs(m.lifetime_revenue - r.lifetime_revenue) > 0.01) as model_value, 0 as reference_value

description: Count of customers where lifetime_orders differ between model and reference.
sql: select 'orders_mismatch' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where m.lifetime_orders != r.lifetime_orders) as model_value, 0 as reference_value

description: Count of customers where avg_order_supply_cost differs by more than 0.01 between model and reference.
sql: select 'supply_cost_mismatch' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where abs(coalesce(m.avg_order_supply_cost,-9999) - coalesce(r.avg_order_supply_cost,-9999)) > 0.01) as model_value, 0 as reference_value

description: Grand total of lifetime_revenue
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of lifetime_revenue in the most recent month
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('month', first_order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest month' as slice,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where date_trunc('month', first_order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where date_trunc('month', first_order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Grand total of lifetime_revenue
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of lifetime_revenue in the most recent month
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('month', first_order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest month' as slice,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where date_trunc('month', first_order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where date_trunc('month', first_order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Compares total number of customer rows between model and reference.
sql: select 'total_customers' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output)::double as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output)::double as reference_value

description: Counts customer_id keys present in one table but missing in the other.
sql: select 'key_mismatch_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m where not exists (select 1 from reference_output r where r.customer_id = m.customer_id))::double as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output r where not exists (select 1 from model_output m where m.customer_id = r.customer_id))::double as reference_value

description: Grand total of lifetime_orders across all customers.
sql: select 'total_lifetime_orders' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output)::double as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output)::double as reference_value

description: Grand total of lifetime_revenue across all customers.
sql: select 'total_lifetime_revenue' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output)::double as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output)::double as reference_value

description: Overall revenue-weighted average order value (sum revenue / sum orders) to detect distortion from per-customer averaging.
sql: select 'total_avg_order_value_weighted' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output) / (select sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output) / (select sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Simple mean of the stored avg_order_supply_cost column across customers (ignoring nulls).
sql: select 'total_avg_order_supply_cost_mean' as slice, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from model_output) as model_value, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Order-count-weighted average supply cost, checking that per-customer averages aggregate consistently.
sql: select 'total_avg_order_supply_cost_orderweighted' as slice, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost*lifetime_orders) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) / (select sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as model_value, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost*lifetime_orders) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) / (select sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as reference_value

description: Per-customer lifetime_orders comparison via full outer join on customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.lifetime_orders as model_value, r.lifetime_orders as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Per-customer lifetime_revenue comparison via full outer join on customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.lifetime_revenue as model_value, r.lifetime_revenue as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Per-customer avg_order_value comparison via full outer join on customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.avg_order_value as model_value, r.avg_order_value as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Per-customer avg_order_supply_cost comparison, sensitive to differing treatment of orders with no item records.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.avg_order_supply_cost as model_value, r.avg_order_supply_cost as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Per-customer first_order_date comparison expressed as days since epoch for numeric comparison.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.first_order_date) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.first_order_date) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Per-customer last_order_date comparison expressed as days since epoch for numeric comparison.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.last_order_date) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.last_order_date) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Count of customers grouped by year of first_order_date.
sql: select cast(extract(year from coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) as varchar) as slice, count(m.customer_id) as model_value, count(r.customer_id) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Sum of lifetime_revenue grouped by year of first_order_date.
sql: select cast(extract(year from coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) as varchar) as slice, sum(m.lifetime_revenue) as model_value, sum(r.lifetime_revenue) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Sum of lifetime_revenue grouped by year-month of first_order_date.
sql: select strftime(coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date), '%Y-%m') as slice, sum(m.lifetime_revenue) as model_value, sum(r.lifetime_revenue) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Sum of lifetime_revenue grouped by year-month of last_order_date, exposing trailing-period discrepancies.
sql: select strftime(coalesce(m.last_order_date, r.last_order_date), '%Y-%m') as slice, sum(m.lifetime_revenue) as model_value, sum(r.lifetime_revenue) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Sum of lifetime_orders grouped by year-quarter of first_order_date.
sql: select cast(extract(year from coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) as varchar) || '-Q' || cast(date_part('quarter', coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) as varchar) as slice, sum(m.lifetime_orders) as model_value, sum(r.lifetime_orders) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Count of customers grouped by week (truncated) of first_order_date.
sql: select cast(date_trunc('week', coalesce(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) as varchar) as slice, count(m.customer_id) as model_value, count(r.customer_id) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1 order by 1

description: Earliest first_order_date in each dataset, as days since epoch.
sql: select 'min_first_order_date' as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select min(first_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select min(first_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Latest last_order_date in each dataset, as days since epoch.
sql: select 'max_last_order_date' as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select max(last_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select max(last_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Number of customers whose first_order_date equals the earliest date in each dataset.
sql: select 'first_period_customers' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where first_order_date = (select min(first_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where first_order_date = (select min(first_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Total lifetime_revenue for customers whose first_order_date equals the earliest date in each dataset.
sql: select 'first_period_revenue' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where first_order_date = (select min(first_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where first_order_date = (select min(first_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Number of customers whose last_order_date equals the latest date in each dataset.
sql: select 'last_period_customers' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where last_order_date = (select max(last_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where last_order_date = (select max(last_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Total lifetime_revenue for customers whose last_order_date equals the latest date in each dataset.
sql: select 'last_period_revenue' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where last_order_date = (select max(last_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where last_order_date = (select max(last_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Counts rows where stored avg_order_value does not equal lifetime_revenue/lifetime_orders within tolerance, in each dataset.
sql: select 'avg_order_value_mismatch_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_orders > 0 and abs(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue / lifetime_orders) > 0.01) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_orders > 0 and abs(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue / lifetime_orders) > 0.01) as reference_value

description: Counts customers with a null avg_order_supply_cost, checking consistent handling of orders with no item records.
sql: select 'null_avg_order_supply_cost_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as reference_value

description: Counts customers with lifetime_orders <= 0, which should not occur given the qualifying-order business rule.
sql: select 'nonpositive_lifetime_orders_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_orders <= 0) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_orders <= 0) as reference_value

description: Sum of lifetime_revenue grouped by customer_name, exposing naming or dedup inconsistencies.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_name, r.customer_name) as slice, sum(m.lifetime_revenue) as model_value, sum(r.lifetime_revenue) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1

description: Compares the count of distinct customer_name values between the two datasets.
sql: select 'distinct_customer_name_count' as slice, (select count(distinct customer_name) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(distinct customer_name) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Counts customers in lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+) to detect fan-out inflation of order counts.
sql: select case when coalesce(m.lifetime_orders, r.lifetime_orders) = 1 then '1_order' when coalesce(m.lifetime_orders, r.lifetime_orders) between 2 and 5 then '2-5_orders' when coalesce(m.lifetime_orders, r.lifetime_orders) between 6 and 10 then '6-10_orders' else '11+_orders' end as slice, count(m.customer_id) as model_value, count(r.customer_id) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id group by 1

description: Compares the total number of customer rows between model and reference.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares grand total lifetime_revenue across all customers.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares grand total lifetime_orders across all customers.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares overall order-weighted average order value (sum revenue / sum orders) to catch averaging errors.
sql: select 'total_weighted' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue)/sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue)/sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares the simple mean of per-customer avg_order_supply_cost, ignoring nulls, across all customers.
sql: select 'total_simple_mean' as slice, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from model_output) as model_value, (select avg(avg_order_supply_cost) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares the count of distinct customer_id keys between model and reference to detect duplicate or missing keys.
sql: select 'distinct_customer_count' as slice, (select count(distinct customer_id) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(distinct customer_id) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Checks for duplicate customer_id rows by comparing total rows minus distinct keys in each table.
sql: select 'duplicate_rows' as slice, (select count(*) - count(distinct customer_id) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(*) - count(distinct customer_id) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Counts customer_id keys present in reference but absent from model output.
sql: with j as (select m.customer_id as m_id, r.customer_id as r_id from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id) select 'missing_in_model' as slice, cast(0 as bigint) as model_value, sum(case when m_id is null and r_id is not null then 1 else 0 end) as reference_value from j

description: Counts customer_id keys present in model but absent from reference output.
sql: with j as (select m.customer_id as m_id, r.customer_id as r_id from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id) select 'missing_in_reference' as slice, sum(case when r_id is null and m_id is not null then 1 else 0 end) as model_value, cast(0 as bigint) as reference_value from j

description: Compares lifetime_revenue per customer, full outer joined on customer_id to surface mismatches and missing keys.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.lifetime_revenue as model_value, r.lifetime_revenue as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares lifetime_orders per customer, full outer joined on customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.lifetime_orders as model_value, r.lifetime_orders as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares avg_order_value per customer, full outer joined on customer_id.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.avg_order_value as model_value, r.avg_order_value as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares avg_order_supply_cost per customer, full outer joined on customer_id, exposing null-handling differences.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, m.avg_order_supply_cost as model_value, r.avg_order_supply_cost as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares first_order_date per customer (as days since epoch) to catch date boundary or timezone truncation errors.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.first_order_date) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.first_order_date) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares last_order_date per customer (as days since epoch) to catch date boundary or timezone truncation errors.
sql: select coalesce(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.last_order_date) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.last_order_date) as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue bucketed by the calendar month of each customer's first_order_date.
sql: with mm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mm.mon, rm.mon) as slice, mm.rev as model_value, rm.rev as reference_value from mm full outer join rm on mm.mon = rm.mon order by 1

description: Compares count of customers bucketed by the calendar month of each customer's first_order_date.
sql: with mm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, count(*) as cnt from model_output group by 1), rm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, count(*) as cnt from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mm.mon, rm.mon) as slice, mm.cnt as model_value, rm.cnt as reference_value from mm full outer join rm on mm.mon = rm.mon order by 1

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue bucketed by the calendar month of each customer's last_order_date.
sql: with mm as (select strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rm as (select strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') as mon, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mm.mon, rm.mon) as slice, mm.rev as model_value, rm.rev as reference_value from mm full outer join rm on mm.mon = rm.mon order by 1

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue bucketed by the calendar year of each customer's first_order_date.
sql: with mm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y') as yr, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rm as (select strftime(first_order_date, '%Y') as yr, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mm.yr, rm.yr) as slice, mm.rev as model_value, rm.rev as reference_value from mm full outer join rm on mm.yr = rm.yr order by 1

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue bucketed by the calendar quarter of each customer's first_order_date.
sql: with mq as (select cast(date_part('year', first_order_date) as varchar) || '-Q' || cast(date_part('quarter', first_order_date) as varchar) as q, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rq as (select cast(date_part('year', first_order_date) as varchar) || '-Q' || cast(date_part('quarter', first_order_date) as varchar) as q, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mq.q, rq.q) as slice, mq.rev as model_value, rq.rev as reference_value from mq full outer join rq on mq.q = rq.q order by 1

description: Compares the earliest first_order_date across all customers (as days since epoch) to catch boundary truncation issues.
sql: select 'min_first_order_date' as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select min(first_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select min(first_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Compares the latest last_order_date across all customers (as days since epoch) to catch boundary truncation issues.
sql: select 'max_last_order_date' as slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select max(last_order_date) from model_output)) as model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (select max(last_order_date) from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue attributed to the earliest calendar month of first orders in each table.
sql: select 'earliest_month_revenue' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(min(first_order_date), '%Y-%m') from model_output)) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(min(first_order_date), '%Y-%m') from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue attributed to the latest calendar month of last orders in each table.
sql: select 'latest_month_revenue' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from model_output where strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(max(last_order_date), '%Y-%m') from model_output)) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) from reference_output where strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(max(last_order_date), '%Y-%m') from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Compares the count of customers whose last_order_date falls in the most recent calendar month in each table.
sql: select 'latest_month_customer_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(max(last_order_date), '%Y-%m') from model_output)) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') = (select strftime(max(last_order_date), '%Y-%m') from reference_output)) as reference_value

description: Compares the count of customers with exactly one lifetime order, an edge case for avg_order_value calculation.
sql: select 'single_order_customers_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as reference_value

description: Compares the mean avg_order_value among single-order customers, where avg_order_value should equal order_total.
sql: select 'single_order_avg_order_value_mean' as slice, (select avg(avg_order_value) from model_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as model_value, (select avg(avg_order_value) from reference_output where lifetime_orders = 1) as reference_value

description: Compares the count of customers with a null avg_order_supply_cost, testing the 'exclude orders with no item records rather than count as zero' rule.
sql: select 'null_avg_order_supply_cost_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is null) as reference_value

description: Checks internal consistency of each table by comparing the gap between summed lifetime_revenue and summed (avg_order_value * lifetime_orders).
sql: select 'revenue_minus_avg_times_orders' as slice, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) - sum(avg_order_value * lifetime_orders) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(lifetime_revenue) - sum(avg_order_value * lifetime_orders) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compares the order-count-weighted average of avg_order_supply_cost across customers, distinct from the simple per-customer mean.
sql: select 'total_weighted_supply_cost' as slice, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) / sum(lifetime_orders) from model_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as model_value, (select sum(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) / sum(lifetime_orders) from reference_output where avg_order_supply_cost is not null) as reference_value

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped into lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+).
sql: with mb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from model_output group by 1), rb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, sum(lifetime_revenue) as rev from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mb.bucket, rb.bucket) as slice, mb.rev as model_value, rb.rev as reference_value from mb full outer join rb on mb.bucket = rb.bucket

description: Compares the count of customers grouped into lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+).
sql: with mb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as cnt from model_output group by 1), rb as (select case when lifetime_orders = 1 then '1' when lifetime_orders between 2 and 5 then '2-5' when lifetime_orders between 6 and 10 then '6-10' else '11+' end as bucket, count(*) as cnt from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(mb.bucket, rb.bucket) as slice, mb.cnt as model_value, rb.cnt as reference_value from mb full outer join rb on mb.bucket = rb.bucket

description: Counts customer_id keys that match between tables but have differing customer_name values, expecting zero mismatches.
sql: select 'name_mismatch_count' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output m join reference_output r on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where m.customer_name <> r.customer_name) as model_value, cast(0 as bigint) as reference_value

description: Compares lifetime_revenue for the top 10 customers by reference revenue, to verify high-value accounts are not distorted.
sql: with top10 as (select customer_id from reference_output order by lifetime_revenue desc limit 10) select r.customer_id as slice, m.lifetime_revenue as model_value, r.lifetime_revenue as reference_value from reference_output r left join model_output m on m.customer_id = r.customer_id where r.customer_id in (select customer_id from top10)

description: Compares total row counts between model and reference outputs.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares distinct customer_id counts to catch duplicate or missing keys.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares grand total lifetime_revenue across all customers.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares grand total lifetime_orders across all customers.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares the revenue-weighted average order value (sum revenue / sum orders) at the grand total level.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue)/NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders),0) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue)/NULLIF(SUM(lifetime_orders),0) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares the simple (unweighted) average of per-customer avg_order_supply_cost, ignoring customers with no item records.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Flags customer_id keys present in one table but missing from the other.
sql: SELECT 'in_model_not_reference' AS slice, COUNT(*) AS model_value, 0 AS reference_value FROM model_output m LEFT JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE r.customer_id IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT 'in_reference_not_model' AS slice, 0 AS model_value, COUNT(*) AS reference_value FROM reference_output r LEFT JOIN model_output m ON r.customer_id = m.customer_id WHERE m.customer_id IS NULL

description: Compares lifetime_revenue per customer_id, catching duplicate-key fan-out via SUM.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares lifetime_orders per customer_id, catching duplicate-key fan-out via SUM.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares avg_order_value per customer_id.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(avg_order_value) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(avg_order_value) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares avg_order_supply_cost per customer_id, sensitive to incorrect exclusion/inclusion of orders without item records.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares first_order_date (as epoch days) per customer_id.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(first_order_date) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, MIN(first_order_date) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, CAST(m.val - DATE '1970-01-01' AS BIGINT) AS model_value, CAST(r.val - DATE '1970-01-01' AS BIGINT) AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares last_order_date (as epoch days) per customer_id.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT customer_id, MAX(last_order_date) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT customer_id, MAX(last_order_date) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, CAST(m.val - DATE '1970-01-01' AS BIGINT) AS model_value, CAST(r.val - DATE '1970-01-01' AS BIGINT) AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped by year of first_order_date.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y') AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y') AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.yr, r.yr) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.yr = r.yr

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped by year-month of first_order_date.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS mo, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS mo, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.mo, r.mo) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped by year-quarter of first_order_date.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((EXTRACT(month FROM first_order_date)-1)/3+1) AS INT) AS q, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((EXTRACT(month FROM first_order_date)-1)/3+1) AS INT) AS q, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.q, r.q) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.q = r.q

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue grouped by year of last_order_date.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y') AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y') AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.yr, r.yr) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.yr = r.yr

description: Compares total lifetime_orders grouped by year-month of last_order_date.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS mo, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS mo, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.mo, r.mo) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo

description: Compares customer counts on the earliest first_order_date (per reference) to check boundary handling.
sql: WITH ref_min AS (SELECT MIN(first_order_date) AS d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'first_order_date_min=' || CAST(d AS VARCHAR) AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE first_order_date = ref_min.d) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE first_order_date = ref_min.d) AS reference_value FROM ref_min

description: Compares customer counts on the latest last_order_date (per reference) to check boundary handling.
sql: WITH ref_max AS (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) AS d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'last_order_date_max=' || CAST(d AS VARCHAR) AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE last_order_date = ref_max.d) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE last_order_date = ref_max.d) AS reference_value FROM ref_max

description: Compares summed avg_order_value for one-order customers, an edge case for the avg_order_value formula.
sql: SELECT 'lifetime_orders=1' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_value) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_value) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS reference_value

description: Compares the count of customers with a null avg_order_supply_cost, testing correct exclusion of customers with no item records.
sql: SELECT 'null_avg_order_supply_cost' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NULL) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NULL) AS reference_value

description: Compares customer counts across lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-3, 4-10, 11+).
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders=1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 4 AND 10 THEN '4-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders=1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 4 AND 10 THEN '4-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.bucket, r.bucket) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.bucket = r.bucket

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue across lifetime_orders buckets (1, 2-3, 4-10, 11+).
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders=1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 4 AND 10 THEN '4-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders=1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 3 THEN '2-3' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 4 AND 10 THEN '4-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.bucket, r.bucket) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.bucket = r.bucket

description: Counts customer_id keys present in both tables whose customer_name differs; expected to be zero.
sql: SELECT 'name_mismatch_count' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output m JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE m.customer_name IS DISTINCT FROM r.customer_name) AS model_value, 0 AS reference_value

description: Compares min/max first_order_date and last_order_date (as epoch days) between model and reference.
sql: SELECT 'min_first_order_date' AS slice, (SELECT MIN(first_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT MIN(first_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM reference_output) AS reference_value UNION ALL SELECT 'max_first_order_date' AS slice, (SELECT MAX(first_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT MAX(first_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM reference_output) AS reference_value UNION ALL SELECT 'min_last_order_date' AS slice, (SELECT MIN(last_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT MIN(last_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM reference_output) AS reference_value UNION ALL SELECT 'max_last_order_date' AS slice, (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) - DATE '1970-01-01' FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Compares the count of customers with lifetime_revenue <= 0, an unexpected edge case given qualifying-order filters.
sql: SELECT 'revenue_lte_0' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_revenue <= 0) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_revenue <= 0) AS reference_value

description: Compares total lifetime_revenue by week of last_order_date for the most recent 8 weeks (per reference max date), testing recency edge handling.
sql: WITH ref_max AS (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) AS d FROM reference_output), m AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', last_order_date) AS wk, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM model_output, ref_max WHERE last_order_date > ref_max.d - INTERVAL 56 DAY GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', last_order_date) AS wk, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS val FROM reference_output, ref_max WHERE last_order_date > ref_max.d - INTERVAL 56 DAY GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.wk AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.wk AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk

description: Compares the count of rows where stored avg_order_value deviates from recomputed lifetime_revenue/lifetime_orders by more than a small epsilon.
sql: SELECT 'avg_order_value_inconsistent_rows' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE ABS(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue / NULLIF(lifetime_orders, 0)) > 0.01) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE ABS(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue / NULLIF(lifetime_orders, 0)) > 0.01) AS reference_value

description: Compares a weighted total proxy (sum of avg_order_supply_cost times lifetime_orders) to surface systematic supply-cost averaging errors.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_supply_cost * lifetime_orders) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Grand total of order_count
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of order_count in the most recent day
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('day', order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest day' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Grand total of order_count
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of order_count in the most recent day
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('day', order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest day' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Grand total order_count across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Grand total of daily customer_count summed across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(customer_count) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(customer_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Grand total item_count across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(item_count) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(item_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Grand total revenue_gross across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(revenue_gross) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(revenue_gross) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Order-count-weighted average of avg_items_per_order across all days, as an overall sanity check.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select sum(avg_items_per_order*order_count)/nullif(sum(order_count),0) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(avg_items_per_order*order_count)/nullif(sum(order_count),0) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total number of day-rows present in each table.
sql: select 'total' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Dates present in only one of the two tables (key coverage gap check).

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(order_date, '%m') AS moy, sum(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(order_date, '%m') AS moy, sum(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.moy, r.moy) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.moy = r.moy ORDER BY 1

description: order_count on the earliest order_date present in each table (edge period check).
sql: SELECT 'first_date_order_count' AS slice, (SELECT order_count FROM model_output ORDER BY order_date ASC LIMIT 1) AS model_value, (SELECT order_count FROM reference_output ORDER BY order_date ASC LIMIT 1) AS reference_value

description: order_count on the latest order_date present in each table (edge period check).
sql: SELECT 'last_date_order_count' AS slice, (SELECT order_count FROM model_output ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS model_value, (SELECT order_count FROM reference_output ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 1) AS reference_value

description: Earliest order_date in each table, expressed as days since epoch, to detect boundary/truncation differences.
sql: SELECT 'min_order_date' AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT min(order_date) FROM model_output)) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT min(order_date) FROM reference_output)) AS reference_value

description: Latest order_date in each table, expressed as days since epoch, to detect boundary/truncation differences.
sql: SELECT 'max_order_date' AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT max(order_date) FROM model_output)) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT max(order_date) FROM reference_output)) AS reference_value

description: Overall revenue per order (sum revenue_gross / sum order_count) compared between model and reference.
sql: SELECT 'revenue_per_order' AS slice, (SELECT sum(revenue_gross)*1.0/sum(order_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT sum(revenue_gross)*1.0/sum(order_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Overall customers per order (sum customer_count / sum order_count) compared between model and reference, exposing join fan-out or dedup differences.
sql: SELECT 'customers_per_order' AS slice, (SELECT sum(customer_count)*1.0/sum(order_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT sum(customer_count)*1.0/sum(order_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Grand total order_count across all days, model vs reference.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(order_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(order_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Grand total of daily customer_count summed across all days.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(customer_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(customer_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Grand total item_count across all days.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(item_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(item_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Grand total revenue_gross across all days.
sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(revenue_gross) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(revenue_gross) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Simple (unweighted) average of the daily avg_items_per_order values, nulls skipped.
sql: SELECT 'total_unweighted' AS slice, (SELECT AVG(avg_items_per_order) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT AVG(avg_items_per_order) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Order-count-weighted average of avg_items_per_order across all days (approximation using daily order_count as weight).
sql: SELECT 'total_weighted' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count)/SUM(order_count) FROM model_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count)/SUM(order_count) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL) AS reference_value

description: Count of distinct order_date rows in each table.
sql: SELECT 'row_count_days' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_date) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_date) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Count of order_date keys present only in model vs only in reference.
sql: WITH only_model AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM model_output m WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reference_output r WHERE r.order_date = m.order_date)), only_ref AS (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM reference_output r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM model_output m WHERE m.order_date = r.order_date)) SELECT 'dates_only_in_model' AS slice, (SELECT cnt FROM only_model) AS model_value, 0 AS reference_value UNION ALL SELECT 'dates_only_in_reference' AS slice, 0 AS model_value, (SELECT cnt FROM only_ref) AS reference_value

description: Per-day order_count, full outer join to expose missing dates on either side.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT order_date, order_count FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT order_date, order_count FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.order_date AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.order_date AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.order_count AS model_value, r.order_count AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.order_date = r.order_date ORDER BY slice

description: Per-day customer_count, full outer join to expose missing dates on either side.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT order_date, customer_count FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT order_date, customer_count FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.order_date AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.order_date AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.customer_count AS model_value, r.customer_count AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.order_date = r.order_date ORDER BY slice

description: Per-day item_count, full outer join to expose missing dates on either side.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT order_date, item_count FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT order_date, item_count FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.order_date AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.order_date AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.item_count AS model_value, r.item_count AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.order_date = r.order_date ORDER BY slice

description: Per-day revenue_gross, full outer join to expose missing dates on either side.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT order_date, revenue_gross FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT order_date, revenue_gross FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.order_date AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.order_date AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.revenue_gross AS model_value, r.revenue_gross AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.order_date = r.order_date ORDER BY slice

description: Per-day avg_items_per_order, full outer join to expose missing dates or diverging averages.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT order_date, avg_items_per_order FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT order_date, avg_items_per_order FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.order_date AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.order_date AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.avg_items_per_order AS model_value, r.avg_items_per_order AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.order_date = r.order_date ORDER BY slice

description: Weekly total order_count (week starting Monday per DuckDB date_trunc).
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.wk, '%Y-%m-%d'), strftime(r.wk, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk ORDER BY slice

description: Weekly total customer_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(customer_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(customer_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.wk, '%Y-%m-%d'), strftime(r.wk, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk ORDER BY slice

description: Weekly total item_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(item_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(item_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.wk, '%Y-%m-%d'), strftime(r.wk, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk ORDER BY slice

description: Weekly total revenue_gross.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.wk, '%Y-%m-%d'), strftime(r.wk, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk ORDER BY slice

description: Weekly order-count-weighted average avg_items_per_order.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count) AS wsum, SUM(order_count) AS ocount FROM model_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', order_date) AS wk, SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count) AS wsum, SUM(order_count) AS ocount FROM reference_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.wk, '%Y-%m-%d'), strftime(r.wk, '%Y-%m-%d')) AS slice, m.wsum / m.ocount AS model_value, r.wsum / r.ocount AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.wk = r.wk ORDER BY slice

description: Monthly total order_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.mo, '%Y-%m'), strftime(r.mo, '%Y-%m')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo ORDER BY slice

description: Monthly total customer_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(customer_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(customer_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.mo, '%Y-%m'), strftime(r.mo, '%Y-%m')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo ORDER BY slice

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(item_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(item_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.mo, '%Y-%m'), strftime(r.mo, '%Y-%m')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo ORDER BY slice

description: Monthly total revenue_gross.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.mo, '%Y-%m'), strftime(r.mo, '%Y-%m')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo ORDER BY slice

description: Monthly order-count-weighted average avg_items_per_order.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count) AS wsum, SUM(order_count) AS ocount FROM model_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', order_date) AS mo, SUM(avg_items_per_order*order_count) AS wsum, SUM(order_count) AS ocount FROM reference_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.mo, '%Y-%m'), strftime(r.mo, '%Y-%m')) AS slice, m.wsum / m.ocount AS model_value, r.wsum / r.ocount AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.mo = r.mo ORDER BY slice

description: Quarterly total order_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS q, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS q, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.q,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((date_part('month', m.q)-1)/3+1) AS VARCHAR), strftime(r.q,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((date_part('month', r.q)-1)/3+1) AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.q = r.q ORDER BY slice

description: Quarterly total revenue_gross.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS q, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', order_date) AS q, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.q,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((date_part('month', m.q)-1)/3+1) AS VARCHAR), strftime(r.q,'%Y') || '-Q' || CAST(((date_part('month', r.q)-1)/3+1) AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.q = r.q ORDER BY slice

description: Yearly total order_count.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('year', order_date) AS yr, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('year', order_date) AS yr, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.yr,'%Y'), strftime(r.yr,'%Y')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.yr = r.yr ORDER BY slice

description: Yearly total revenue_gross.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_trunc('year', order_date) AS yr, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_trunc('year', order_date) AS yr, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(strftime(m.yr,'%Y'), strftime(r.yr,'%Y')) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.yr = r.yr ORDER BY slice

description: order_count on the earliest order_date present in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'first_day' AS slice, (SELECT order_count FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT first_d FROM bounds)) AS model_value, (SELECT order_count FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT first_d FROM bounds)) AS reference_value

description: order_count on the latest order_date present in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT MAX(order_date) AS last_d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'last_day' AS slice, (SELECT order_count FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT last_d FROM bounds)) AS model_value, (SELECT order_count FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT last_d FROM bounds)) AS reference_value

description: revenue_gross on the earliest order_date present in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'first_day' AS slice, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT first_d FROM bounds)) AS model_value, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT first_d FROM bounds)) AS reference_value

description: revenue_gross on the latest order_date present in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT MAX(order_date) AS last_d FROM reference_output) SELECT 'last_day' AS slice, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT last_d FROM bounds)) AS model_value, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT last_d FROM bounds)) AS reference_value

description: revenue_gross on the day with the highest revenue in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH peak AS (SELECT order_date FROM reference_output ORDER BY revenue_gross DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT 'peak_revenue_day' AS slice, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT order_date FROM peak)) AS model_value, (SELECT revenue_gross FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT order_date FROM peak)) AS reference_value

description: order_count on the day with the highest order_count in the reference dashboard.
sql: WITH peak AS (SELECT order_date FROM reference_output ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 1) SELECT 'peak_order_count_day' AS slice, (SELECT order_count FROM model_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT order_date FROM peak)) AS model_value, (SELECT order_count FROM reference_output WHERE order_date = (SELECT order_date FROM peak)) AS reference_value

description: Overall ratio of total order_count to total customer_count.
sql: SELECT 'orders_per_customer' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(order_count)*1.0/SUM(customer_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(order_count)*1.0/SUM(customer_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Overall ratio of total revenue_gross to total order_count.
sql: SELECT 'revenue_per_order' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(revenue_gross)*1.0/SUM(order_count) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(revenue_gross)*1.0/SUM(order_count) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

description: Total order_count grouped by day-of-week (0=Sunday..6=Saturday) to catch timezone/day-boundary shifts.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_part('dow', order_date) AS dow, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_part('dow', order_date) AS dow, SUM(order_count) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.dow AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.dow AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.dow = r.dow ORDER BY slice

description: Total revenue_gross grouped by day-of-week to catch timezone/day-boundary shifts.
sql: WITH m AS (SELECT date_part('dow', order_date) AS dow, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT date_part('dow', order_date) AS dow, SUM(revenue_gross) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(CAST(m.dow AS VARCHAR), CAST(r.dow AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.dow = r.dow ORDER BY slice

description: Count of days where avg_items_per_order is NULL (orders-with-no-items edge case), model vs reference.
sql: SELECT 'null_avg_items_days' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NULL) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_items_per_order IS NULL) AS reference_value

description: Count of days where order_count equals zero, which should not occur under the model's business definition.
sql: SELECT 'zero_order_count_days' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE order_count = 0) AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE order_count = 0) AS reference_value

description: Grand total of order_count
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of order_count in the most recent day
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('day', order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest day' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Grand total of order_count
sql:
select 'grand_total' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Total of order_count in the most recent day
sql:
with latest as (select max(date_trunc('day', order_date)) as p from reference_output)
select 'latest day' as slice,
  (select sum(order_count) from model_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as model_value,
  (select sum(order_count) from reference_output where date_trunc('day', order_date) = (select p from latest)) as reference_value

description: Compare total order_count across all days between model and reference.
sql: select 'total' as slice, sum(order_count) as model_value, null as reference_value from model_output union all select 'total', null, sum(order_count) from reference_output

description: Compare total customer_count sum across all days (note: not deduped across days, just sanity sum).
sql: select 'total' as slice, sum(customer_count) as model_value, null as reference_value from model_output union all select 'total', null, sum(customer_count) from reference_output

description: Compare total item_count across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, sum(item_count) as model_value, null as reference_value from model_output union all select 'total', null, sum(item_count) from reference_output

description: Compare total revenue_gross across all days.
sql: select 'total' as slice, sum(revenue_gross) as model_value, null as reference_value from model_output union all select 'total', null, sum(revenue_gross) from reference_output

description: Compare total number of day rows present in each table.
sql: select 'total_rows' as slice, (select count(*) from model_output) as model_value, (select count(*) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compare overall weighted average items per order (item_count/order_count) across all days to detect averaging distortion.
sql: select 'overall_avg' as slice, (select sum(item_count)*1.0/sum(order_count) from model_output) as model_value, (select sum(item_count)*1.0/sum(order_count) from reference_output) as reference_value

description: Compare order_count for every calendar day, full outer join on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.order_count as model_value, r.order_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare customer_count for every calendar day.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.customer_count as model_value, r.customer_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare item_count for every calendar day.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.item_count as model_value, r.item_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare revenue_gross for every calendar day.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.revenue_gross as model_value, r.revenue_gross as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare avg_items_per_order for every calendar day to detect null-handling discrepancies.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.avg_items_per_order as model_value, r.avg_items_per_order as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare order_count aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(order_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(order_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare item_count aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(item_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(item_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare revenue_gross aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(revenue_gross) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(revenue_gross) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare order_count aggregated by calendar month.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('month', order_date) as mo, sum(order_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('month', order_date) as mo, sum(order_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.mo as varchar), cast(r.mo as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.mo = r.mo order by 1

description: Compare customer_count sum aggregated by calendar month.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('month', order_date) as mo, sum(customer_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('month', order_date) as mo, sum(customer_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.mo as varchar), cast(r.mo as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.mo = r.mo order by 1

description: Compare item_count aggregated by calendar month.

description: Full outer join on order_date to find dates present in only one side (missing dates show as NULL on the other side).
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, case when m.order_date is not null then 1 else null end as model_value, case when r.order_date is not null then 1 else null end as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date where m.order_date is null or r.order_date is null order by 1

description: Compare order_count for every day, full outer joined on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.order_count as model_value, r.order_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare customer_count for every day, full outer joined on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.customer_count as model_value, r.customer_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare item_count for every day, full outer joined on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.item_count as model_value, r.item_count as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare revenue_gross for every day, full outer joined on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.revenue_gross as model_value, r.revenue_gross as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare avg_items_per_order for every day, full outer joined on order_date.
sql: select coalesce(cast(m.order_date as varchar), cast(r.order_date as varchar)) as slice, m.avg_items_per_order as model_value, r.avg_items_per_order as reference_value from model_output m full outer join reference_output r on m.order_date = r.order_date order by 1

description: Compare order_count aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(order_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(order_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare revenue_gross aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(revenue_gross) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(revenue_gross) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare item_count aggregated by ISO week.
sql: with m as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(item_count) as v from model_output group by 1), r as (select date_trunc('week', order_date) as wk, sum(item_count) as v from reference_output group by 1) select coalesce(cast(m.wk as varchar), cast(r.wk as varchar)) as slice, m.v as model_value, r.v as reference_value from m full outer join r on m.wk = r.wk order by 1

description: Compare order_count aggregated by calendar month.
